$comment: GATING FOR v2 DESCRIPTION TRANSPORT. Resolves the freeze-order substrate problem without relaxing the mailbox prohibition and without a transcription boundary. Names the committer and the attestation form. Touches no frozen artifact and no running job.

binding_for_this_document.note: Stated rather than blank, per the standing rule.

THE_SUBSTRATE_PROBLEM_IS_REAL.their_finding: RULING_3 requires the description's FREEZE COMMIT to precede the first corpus-authoring commit in git history. The PM's description is being written into the mailbox, and the mailbox has a standing prohibition on ever being copied into a git archive. THE DESCRIPTION HAS NO COMMIT AT ALL, so there is nothing for git history to order.
THE_SUBSTRATE_PROBLEM_IS_REAL.verdict: CORRECT. The rule is right and its substrate did not exist. I ruled an ordering over a thing that is not in the ordered space.
THE_SUBSTRATE_PROBLEM_IS_REAL.their_distinction_is_also_correct: The description CONTENT entering the repository as a versioned artifact is NOT the same act as copying the mailbox. What must be forbidden is THE TRANSPORT, NOT THE TEXT.
THE_SUBSTRATE_PROBLEM_IS_REAL.and_their_worry_about_the_consequence_is: That distinction reintroduces a TRANSCRIPTION BOUNDARY -- the authorship-versus-transcription problem already hit on the researcher slot, now at exactly the point the binding rule exists to protect. A hand transcription can drift, and every downstream digest would verify perfectly against a text that is not what the PM wrote.

RULING_1_DO_NOT_PROVE_THE_TRANSCRIPTION_.their_mitigation: The PM reports the SHA-256 of their own description bytes; the repository artifact is compared byte-for-byte against that digest, so the transcription is PROVED rather than TRUSTED.
RULING_1_DO_NOT_PROVE_THE_TRANSCRIPTION_.why_that_is_nearly_right_and_fails_in_a_: A byte-for-byte comparison ACROSS A FORMAT BOUNDARY will fail for legitimate reasons. The description sits inside a JSON report; the repository artifact is a file. JSON escaping, encoding and line endings differ between the two representations, so the PM's digest of their source text and the digest of the committed file WILL legitimately disagree.
RULING_1_DO_NOT_PROVE_THE_TRANSCRIPTION_.THE_HAZARD_THAT_CREATES: The obvious fix when the comparison fails is to RECOMPUTE THE DIGEST ON THE DESTINATION. That makes the check pass and DESTROYS THE ATTESTATION -- the artifact would then be attested against itself, which is the tautology already ruled against for the prompt-set constants. And it would be done by someone trying to make a legitimate failure go away.
RULING_1_DO_NOT_PROVE_THE_TRANSCRIPTION_.THE_RULING: USE report_path. THE MAILBOX ALREADY HAS THE MECHANISM AND IT DISSOLVES THE PROBLEM RATHER THAN MITIGATING IT.

the_mechanism.source: README: 'report_path, when present, points at a local hash-bound report; the mailbox does not copy its potentially large contents.' It is a validated optional field in the closed schema.
the_mechanism.how_it_applies: The PM writes the description AS THE ARTIFACT'S EXACT FILE BYTES to a local file. The mailbox report carries report_path plus the sha256 of that file in artifacts. THE MAILBOX NEVER CARRIES THE CONTENT, so the prohibition is untouched. The committer copies THE FILE, byte-for-byte.
the_mechanism.what_this_eliminates: THERE IS NO TRANSCRIPTION. Only transport of a file whose digest was computed on the same bytes that land in the repository. A mismatch is then unambiguously a real defect rather than a format artifact.

RULING_1_DO_NOT_PROVE_THE_TRANSCRIPTION_.consequence_for_the_PM: The PM authors THE FILE, not prose to be rendered into a file. What they write is what is committed. That is a small constraint on them and it removes the entire class.

RULING_2_THE_COMMITTER.their_reasoning_confirmed: Not the PM -- barred from repository files, and a description author with repository access can adjust the artifact to match a corpus instead of the reverse, which is the separation of duties already frozen. Not the coordinator -- they do not implement. Therefore an engineer lane.
RULING_2_THE_COMMITTER.THE_PRINCIPLE_THEY_NOTICED_AND_I_AM_STAT: THE COMMITTER IS A THIRD PARTY WHO AUTHORED NEITHER THE DESCRIPTION NOR THE CORPUS. That follows from the separation already ruled and had never been said.
RULING_2_THE_COMMITTER.THE_CONSTRAINT_THAT_MAKES_IT_WORK: THE COMMITTER HAS NO AUTHORITY TO EDIT THE CONTENT. Their entire function is: copy the bytes, recompute the digest, compare to the PM's attested value.
RULING_2_THE_COMMITTER.ON_MISMATCH_THEY_STOP: A digest mismatch is REPORTED, NOT REPAIRED. The committer may not adjust whitespace, re-encode, normalise line endings, or 'fix' anything to make the comparison pass. A committer who can fix a mismatch IS the transcription problem with extra steps.
RULING_2_THE_COMMITTER.why_that_is_the_load_bearing_line: Every failure in this sprint's catalogue that survived review did so because someone with the ability to make a check pass encountered a check that was failing. Removing the ability is stronger than requiring the restraint.

RULING_3_THE_FREEZE_ORDER_NOW_HAS_ITS_SU.resolved: With report_path transport, the description acquires A REAL COMMIT -- the byte-copied artifact -- so git history can order it and RULING_3 of the prior artifact is executable as written.
the_full_ordering_and_what_evidences_eac: 1. PM authors the description file locally and posts report_path plus its sha256. THE MAILBOX REPORT'S timestamp and sequence date the description.
2. The committer copies the file and commits it, after verifying the digest. THE COMMIT is the freeze.

3. Corpus authoring begins. ITS FIRST COMMIT MUST BE A DESCENDANT of the description's freeze commit -- checkable with merge-base --is-ancestor plus distinctness, the same test already used for every chain in this project.
RULING_3_THE_FREEZE_ORDER_NOW_HAS_ITS_SU.unchanged: Any change to the description after step 2 invalidates the corpus built from it, exactly as a prompt edit invalidates activations.

ACCEPTED_WITHOUT_QUALIFICATION.quality_is_not_safety: Their formulation of why it is dangerous rather than merely wrong is better than mine and I adopt it: EACH ASSESSMENT FEELS LIKE IT DISCHARGES THE OTHER -- having established that something is good, the question of whether it is safe feels already answered. That is what makes it a trap rather than an oversight, and it generalises past this sprint and past this project.
ACCEPTED_WITHOUT_QUALIFICATION.ruling_2_rediscovery: They record that they did not know they were restating the suppress_disposition principle, and would rather that be noted than claim the rediscovery as novel. Recorded. Independent rediscovery at a different layer is stronger evidence of generality than a deliberate restatement would have been.
ACCEPTED_WITHOUT_QUALIFICATION.no_resequenced_repeat_to_la_b: Correct. Nothing about the job has changed and a resequenced repeat is what the enrollment rule forbids. Silence from a lane with an unchanged instruction is not a reason to re-issue it.

OPERATIONAL_NOTED_NOT_RULED.job_413287: PENDING on Resources with no node, and the coordinator wants the duration noted rather than assumed. NOTED. A long queue is not evidence of a problem and is not evidence of progress; under fail-closed doctrine it is neither. Nothing downstream may be inferred from it.
OPERATIONAL_NOTED_NOT_RULED.not_mine: Whether to escalate the queue, change the allocation request, or wait is an operator matter.

hard_stops: Copying any mailbox file into a git archive.
Transporting the description as prose to be rendered into a file, rather than as the file's exact bytes via report_path.
Recomputing an attested digest on the destination artifact to make a comparison pass.
A committer who authored the description or the corpus.
A committer editing, re-encoding or normalising content to resolve a digest mismatch. Mismatches are reported, never repaired.
Beginning corpus authoring on a commit that is not a descendant of the description's freeze commit.
